The `acs:create-design` skill must be invoked at least once.

Deterministic and free: this reads the Skill tool call, not the
assistant's prose, so a precondition gate refusing AFTER the skill
routed still counts as a route — which is what this probe asserts.

Why this probe exists: A natural-language request in the skill's domain, never naming the skill. 1.6.0 fixes both halves of a 3/5 split on the 2026-09-13 measurement, neither of them the description's. The prompt said "this epic" and named none: a diagnostic caught the model identifying the right skill ("this matches /acs:create-design exactly") and then declining for want of a referent — "I need to know which epic you mean". It now names the ticket, as ROUTE-create-test-docs and ROUTE-run-e2e-tests already do. And the sandbox is now `epic`: the default `ticketed` profile mints a small, low-stakes TASK, so "design-significant" was false of the only ticket present, while `epic` mints a large, high-stakes epic — exactly what the prompt describes.
